To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nonlinear range correction procedure improves accuracy of the Schmidt and Hunter (S-H) (1978) interactive method for estimating both the mean and standard deviation of population correlations, that it also improves accuracy of the interactive procedure in the homogeneous case (standard deviation of population correlations equal to zero), and that it improves accuracy of the S-H interactive procedure even under extreme violations to the normality assumption.

the nonlinear range correction improves the accuracy of range corrections for population correlations and that the interactive method, with or without nonlinear corrections, provides the most accurate estimates of the mean and standard deviation of population correlations in the absence of extreme violations of the assumption of normality of population correlations.

the new nonlinear range correction procedure improves the accuracy of the S-H interactive method in estimating the mean and SD of population correlations, and that the nonlinear range correction procedure is most accurate in estimating SD when correlations are approximately normally distributed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of estimating the mean (Me ) and the standard deviation (SD) of a population of correlation coefficients (r).
the accuracy of the range-correction procedure for meta-analysis.
the development of a more accurate range-restriction correction procedure for meta-analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nonlinear range correction is an accurate and robust procedure.
the nonlinear range correction improves the accuracy of the S-H interactive procedure in estimating both population mean (Me) correlations and population standard deviation of correlations (SDP).
the nonlinear range correction procedure should be used in conjunction with the interactive method for estimating the mean correlation in a meta-analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonlinear range correction improves accuracy of the interactive procedure for a wide range of conditions.
the nonlinear range correction procedure is recommended for use in meta-analysis.
the nonlinear correction procedure improves the accuracy of the S-H interactive method, even when there are violations of normality and homogeneity assumptions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the range correction procedure can improve the estimation of population parameters, but it is not a panacea.
the range correction procedure is more robust to departures from normality than the interactive method.
the nonlinear correction is the most accurate of all the methods examined.
